title: Stacy Keach, Star of ‘Mike Hammer,’ ‘Fat City,’ Dies at 85
content:
ByCarmel Dagan

Staff Writer

Stacy Keach, a commanding actor whose work includes movies like “Fat City” and the starring role in “The New Mike Hammer” series on CBS, died Tuesday in Poland. He was 85.

His wife, Małgosia Tomassi, confirmed his death toVariety. In a statement, she said he died “after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure” at the family’s home in Magdalenka, Poland.

“Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family,” the statement said. “His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives. But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever.

Active on stage, film and TV into his eighties, he popped up in “The Bourne Legacy,” “Nebraska,” “Two and a Half Men,” “Ray Donovan” and had a recurring voice role on “The Simpsons.” Keach was also known for playing Cardinal Kevin Kearns on “Blue Bloods.” His TV appearances included “Man With a Plan” and “The Black List.” His final role was in “Jay Kelly” in 2025, as the father of Jay Kelly, played by George Clooney.

In 2010, he received a Helen Hayes award for his performance of “King Lear,” for Shakespeare Theater Co., one of many stage honors over the course of his career.

Keach got his Tony nomination for playing Buffalo Bill in the 1969 Broadway production “Indians” early on but garnered even more fame as “Mike Hammer.” The CBS series aired from 1984-87 and he reprised the role in the 1989 TV movie “Mike Hammer: Murder Takes All” and the syndicated series “Mike Hammer, Private Eye” in 1997-98. He also narrated the CNBC series, “American Greed.”

Keach’s run as the private detective got off to a rocky start off screen, however. In 1984, police arrested Keach at London’s Heathrow Airport for possession of cocaine. Pleading guilty, the actor served six months at Reading Prison. Since Keach also narrated “Mike Hammer” in character, impressionist Rich Little was called to sub in as the show’s narrator during Keach’s imprisonment.

In a 2014 television interview, Keach declared that his time in prison was (understandably) the low point of his life, and a friendship he formed with a priest during that time led to his conversion to Roman Catholicism.

Keach’s Emmy nomination came shortly after that period; he was recognized in 1988 for outstanding lead actor in a miniseries or special for playing the famous author of the title in “Ernest Hemingway.”

Part of an acting family that includes his younger brother James, who has gone on to direct and produce, Walter Stacy Keach Jr. was born in Savannah, Ga., the son of actress Mary Cain and Stacy Keach Sr., an actor, drama teacher and theater director. Class president at Van Nuys High School, he graduated from UC Berkeley in 1963, and went on to earn a graduate degree at the Yale School of Drama. He was also a Fulbright Scholar at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art.

In 1966, Keach played the title role in Barbara Garson’s Off Broadway anti-war satire “MacBird!,”winning his first Obie Award. The following year he appeared Off Broadway again, this time with Morgan Freeman (in the latter’s acting debut) in George Tabori’s provocatively titled “The Niggerlovers.”

Keach made his Broadway debut in Georg Buchner’s “Danton’s Death” in 1965, soon thereafter appearing in a revival of “The Country Wife,” followed by the original Broadway production of Bertolt Brecht play “The Caucasian Chalk Circle” and a 1968 staging of “King Lear” in which he played Edmund. The following year he starred in Arthur Kopit’s “Indians,” picking up his Tony nomination for his performance as Buffalo Bill.

He returned to Broadway in 1979 as a replacement for John Wood as Sidney Bruhl in Ira Levin’s long-running mystery comedy “Deathtrap,” starred in “Solitary Confinement” in 1992 and in Robert Schenkkan’s “The Kentucky Cycle” the following year.

Off Broadway, Keach appeared twice in “Hamlet,” in 1964 and 1972, the second time in the title role, winning his second Obie. He also appeared as Falstaff in Henry “IV” Parts I and II in 1968, and as James Tyrone Jr. in O’Neill’s “Long Day’s Journey Into Night” in 1971.

In the early 1980s he starred in the title role of the national touring company of the Cy Coleman musical “Barnum.” He performed the title role in “King Lear” at the Goodman Theater in 2006, and in 2008 played Merlin in a semi-staged version of “Camelot” with the New York Philharmonic.

Keach played Richard M. Nixon in the U.S. traveling version of the play “Frost/Nixon” in 2008 and 2009, in the course of which — one day in March 2009 — he had a series of strokes, from he recovered sufficiently to take another go at “King Lear” in D.C. that summer.

Keach was a founding member of L.A. Theatre Works.

The actor debuted on TV in an episode of college drama “Channing” in 1964, followed by a TV movie versions of Shakespeare’s “The Winter’s Tale” (1967), in which he played Autolycus, and “Macbeth” (1968), in which he played Banquo. Also in 1968 the actor made his big-screen debut in the adaptation of Carson McCullers’ “The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter.”

He played a crippled millionaire in Robert Altman’s “Brewster McCloud” (1970) and by the next year he starred in the title role of the Western “Doc,” playing Doc Holliday opposite Faye Dunaway.

In John Huston’s boxing drama “Fat City” (1972), Keach was the over-the-hill boxer praying for a comeback, and Jeff Bridges was the young boxer on the rise.

Also in 1972 the actor starred with George C. Scott and Jane Alexander in the adaptation of Joseph Wambaugh’s “The New Centurions” and had a supporting role in Huston’s “The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean.” He played in a number of roles before stoner comedy classic “Up in Smoke” (1978).

“The Ninth Configuration” (1980), directed by Willliam Peter Blatty and adapted by him from his own surrealist novel “Twinkle Twinkle ‘Killer’ Kane,” became a cult favorite, with Keach’s as Marine Col. Vincent Kane who runs a hospital for military men with psychiatric problems.

Also in 1980, the actor appeared with his brother James Keach as Frank and Jesse James in “The Long Riders,” and in 1982 he starred with Bruce Dern, Robert Mitchum, Martin Sheen and Paul Sorvino in Jason Miller’s “That Championship Season.”

Additional film credits include Oliver Stone’s biopic “W.” (2008), John Sayles’ “Honeydripper” (2007) and “Sin City: A Dame to Kill For” (2014). He had a recurring role on “ER” and the Fox comedy “Titus.”

H has made numerous guest appearances on shows including “Touched by an Angel,” “Will & Grace,” “George Lopez,” “30 Rock” (as himself), “Anger Management,” “Brooklyn Nine-Nine,” “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit,” “NCIS: New Orleans” and “Hot in Cleveland.”

Keach was married four times, first to Kathryn Baker in 1964, then to Marilyn Aiken from 1975-79 and to Jill Donahue from 1981-86.

He is survived by fourth wife Malgosia Tomassi, whom he married in 1986; son Shannon and daughter Karolina and his brother James Keach.
title_zh: 斯泰西·基奇(Stacy Keach)，電影《麥克·哈默》(Mike Hammer) 和《肥城》(Fat City) 的明星，於85歲時去世。
content_zh:
由卡梅爾·達根(Carmel Dagan)報導

員工撰稿人

斯泰西·基奇(Stacy Keach)，一位具有威嚴的演員，其作品包括電影《肥城》(Fat City)和在CBS播出的《新麥克·哈默》(The New Mike Hammer)系列中的主角，於週二在波蘭去世，享年85歲。

他的妻子瑪爾戈西亞·托馬西(Małgosia Tomassi)向《綜藝雜誌》(Variety)確認了他的死訊。她在聲明中表示，他在波蘭馬格達倫卡(Magdalenka)的家中去世，經歷了“長期而艱難的心臟病和心臟衰竭的鬥爭”。

聲明中提到：“斯泰西不僅是一位傳奇演員，受到全世界觀眾的欣賞和喜愛，更是我摯愛的丈夫，我的伴侶和我們家庭的核心。他的離去在我們的生活中留下了無法估量的空虛。但他非凡的精神，他那令人難忘的聲音，以及他慷慨付出的愛將永遠與我們同在。”

他在舞台、電影和電視上活躍至八十多歲，曾出現在《伯恩的遺產》(The Bourne Legacy)、《內布拉斯加》(Nebraska)、《兩個半男人》(Two and a Half Men)、《雷·多諾萬》(Ray Donovan)中，並在《辛普森家庭》(The Simpsons)中擔任常駐配音角色。基奇還因在《藍血》(Blue Bloods)中飾演基爾恩斯樞機主教而聞名。他的電視出現還包括《計畫男孩》(Man With a Plan)和《黑名單》(The Black List)。他的最後一個角色是在2025年的《傑·凱利》(Jay Kelly)中，飾演由喬治·克隆尼(George Clooney)演出的傑·凱利的父親。

在2010年，他因在莎士比亞劇院公司(Shakespeare Theater Co.)的《李爾王》(King Lear)中的表現獲得海倫·海斯獎(Helen Hayes Award)，這是他職業生涯中眾多舞台榮譽之一。

基奇早期因在1969年百老匯製作的《印第安人》(Indians)中飾演巴法羅·比爾(Buffalo Bill)而獲得托尼獎提名，但他更因飾演“麥克·哈默”(Mike Hammer)而獲得更大的名聲。CBS系列於1984年至1987年播出，他在1989年的電視電影《麥克·哈默：謀殺無所不在》(Mike Hammer: Murder Takes All)和1997至1998年的聯播系列《麥克·哈默，私家偵探》(Mike Hammer, Private Eye)中重返此角色。他還為CNBC系列《美國貪婪》(American Greed)擔任旁白。

然而，基奇作為私家偵探的演出在幕後卻有一段坎坷的開始。1984年，基奇在倫敦希思羅機場因持有可卡因而被警方逮捕。這位演員認罪，並在雷丁監獄(Reading Prison)服刑六個月。由於基奇在角色中也為《麥克·哈默》擔任旁白，模仿藝人瑞奇·利特(Rich Little)在基奇入獄期間被請來代替擔任節目的旁白。

在2014年的一次電視訪談中，基奇表示，他的監禁時間是他人生中的低谷，而他在那段時間與一位神父建立的友誼促使他皈依了羅馬天主教。

基奇的艾美獎提名是在那段時期不久後出現的；他在1988年因在迷你劇或特別節目中飾演著名作家而獲得傑出男主角獎，該劇名為《厄尼斯特·海明威》(Ernest Hemingway)。

沃爾特·斯塔西·基奇二世(Walter Stacy Keach Jr.)出生於喬治亞州薩凡納，來自一個演藝世家，弟弟詹姆斯·基奇(James Keach)後來成為導演和製片人。他是女演員瑪麗·凱恩(Mary Cain)和演員、戲劇教師及劇院導演斯塔西·基奇(Sr.)的兒子。在范奈斯高中的班長，他於1963年畢業於加州大學伯克利分校，隨後在耶魯戲劇學院獲得研究生學位。他還曾是倫敦音樂與戲劇藝術學院的富布賴特學者。

1966年，基奇在芭芭拉·加爾森(Barbara Garson)的百老匯外反戰諷刺劇《麥克鳥！(MacBird!)》中飾演主角，贏得了他的第一個奧比獎(Obie Award)。次年，他再次在百老匯外演出，這次與摩根·弗里曼(Morgan Freeman)合作，後者首次登台，參演喬治·塔博里(George Tabori)挑釁性標題的劇作《黑鬼愛好者(The Niggerlovers)》。

基奇於1965年在喬治·布赫納(Georg Buchner)的《丹頓之死(Danton’s Death)》中首次登上百老匯，隨後參加了《鄉村妻子(The Country Wife)》的復排，接著在伯特霍爾德·布雷希特(Bertolt Brecht)的劇作《高加索灰圈(The Caucasian Chalk Circle)》的原創百老匯製作中演出，並在1968年的《李爾王(King Lear)》中飾演埃德蒙(Edmund)。次年，他在亞瑟·科皮特(Arthur Kopit)的《印第安人(Indians)》中主演，因其在劇中飾演巴法羅·比爾(Buffalo Bill)而獲得托尼獎提名。

1979年，他回到百老匯，接替約翰·伍德(John Wood)飾演艾拉·萊文(Ira Levin)的長壽懸疑喜劇《死亡陷阱(Deathtrap)》中的西德尼·布魯赫(Sidney Bruhl)，1992年主演《孤獨禁閉(Solitary Confinement)》，次年在羅伯特·申肯(Robert Schenkkan)的《肯塔基循環(The Kentucky Cycle)》中演出。

在百老匯外，基奇於1964年和1972年兩次出演《哈姆雷特(Hamlet)》，第二次飾演主角，並贏得了他的第二個奧比獎。他還在1968年出演亨利四世(Henry “IV”)的《法爾斯塔夫(Falstaff)》第一和第二部，並在1971年於奧尼爾(Eugene O’Neill)的《漫長的白天之旅(Long Day’s Journey Into Night)》中飾演詹姆斯·泰隆二世(James Tyrone Jr.)。

在1980年代初，他在全國巡演的賽·科爾曼(Cy Coleman)音樂劇《巴納姆(Barnum)》中主演主角。2006年，他在古德曼劇院(Goodman Theater)演出《李爾王(King Lear)》，2008年則在紐約愛樂樂團(New York Philharmonic)的半舞台版《卡美洛(Camelot)》中飾演梅林(Merlin)。

基奇在2008年和2009年的美國巡演劇《弗羅斯特/尼克森(Frost/Nixon)》中飾演理查德·尼克森(Richard M. Nixon)，在2009年3月的一天，他遭遇了一系列中風，但他恢復得足夠好，於那年夏天在華盛頓特區再次出演《李爾王(King Lear)》。

基奇是洛杉磯劇院作品(L.A. Theatre Works)的創始成員。

這位演員於1964年在大學劇情片《查寧(Channing)》的一集首次登場，隨後在1967年的電視電影版莎士比亞的《冬天的故事(The Winter’s Tale)》中飾演奧托利庫斯(Autolycus)，以及1968年的《麥克白(Macbeth)》中飾演班柯(Banquo)。同年，基奇在改編自卡森·麥卡勒斯(Carson McCullers)的《心是孤獨的獵手(The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter)》中首次登上大銀幕。

他在羅伯特·奧特曼(Robert Altman)的《布魯斯特·麥克勞德(Brewster McCloud)》(1970)中飾演一位殘疾的百萬富翁，次年則在西部片《醫生(Doc)》中主演，與費·唐納薇(Faye Dunaway)搭檔，飾演醫生霍利迪(Doc Holliday)。

在約翰·休斯頓(John Huston)的拳擊劇情片《肥城(Fat City)》(1972)中，基奇(John Keach)飾演一位渴望復出的過氣拳擊手，而傑夫·布里吉斯(Jeff Bridges)則是正在崛起的年輕拳擊手。

同樣在1972年，這位演員與喬治·C·斯科特(George C. Scott)和簡·亞歷山大(Jane Alexander)共同出演了約瑟夫·萬博(Joseph Wambaugh)的改編作品《新世紀警探(The New Centurions)》，並在休斯頓的《羅伊·比恩法官的生活與時代(The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean)》中擔任配角。在經典的嬉皮喜劇《煙霧瀰漫(Up in Smoke)》(1978)之前，他參演了多個角色。

《第九配置(The Ninth Configuration)》(1980)由威廉·彼得·布拉提(William Peter Blatty)執導，並根據他自己超現實主義小說《閃閃發光的‘殺手’凱恩(Twinkle Twinkle ‘Killer’ Kane)》改編，成為了一部邪典電影，基奇飾演的海軍陸戰隊上校文森特·凱恩(Marine Col. Vincent Kane)負責管理一所專門治療有精神問題的軍人的醫院。

同樣在1980年，這位演員與他的兄弟詹姆斯·基奇(James Keach)共同出演了《長途騎士(The Long Riders)》中的法蘭克和傑西·詹姆斯(Frank and Jesse James)，並在1982年與布魯斯·德恩(Bruce Dern)、羅伯特·米徹姆(Robert Mitchum)、馬丁·辛(Martin Sheen)和保羅·索維諾(Paul Sorvino)共同主演了傑森·米勒(Jason Miller)的《冠軍賽季(That Championship Season)》。

他的其他電影作品包括奧利佛·史東(Oliver Stone)的傳記片《W.》(2008)、約翰·塞伊爾斯(John Sayles)的《蜜蜂之歌(Honeydripper)》(2007)以及《罪惡之城：為了殺戮而來的女人(Sin City: A Dame to Kill For)》(2014)。他在《急診室的春天(ER)》和福克斯喜劇《泰特斯(Titus)》中有過常駐角色。

基奇曾結過四次婚，第一次是1964年與凱瑟琳·貝克(Kathryn Baker)結婚，然後是1975年至1979年與瑪麗琳·艾肯(Marilyn Aiken)結婚，接著是1981年至1986年與吉爾·多納休(Jill Donahue)結婚。

他留下了第四任妻子馬爾戈西亞·托馬西(Malgosia Tomassi)，他們於1986年結婚；以及兒子香農(Shannon)、女兒卡羅琳娜(Karolina)和他的兄弟詹姆斯·基奇。
